business_scope.primary_industry_name: Tier-3/4 Server Rack Space Leasing and Bare-Metal Server Hosting

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (1984, as amended by the 2013 and 2018 protocols)
France–China Agreement on the Reciprocal Encouragement and Protection of Investments (signed 2007, in force 2010)
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally applied)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-58 and R.561-1 et seq. as amended by Sapin II Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016; UBO declaration obligations under Article L.561-45 and R.561-20-1 et seq., implemented by Decree No. 2016-1686 of 8 December 2016; UBO register administered by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) within the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) since 1 January 2023; EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD) as transposed.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (restricted to French judicial authorities, TRACFIN, ACPR prudential supervisors, and other designated AML/CFT authorities; general public access restricted in accordance with French law and the CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022, Case C-37/20).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and current registry extract (Kbis or foreign equivalent) of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry or corporate register in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn French translation (traduction assermentée); consular legalization if the origin country is not party to the 1961 Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (mandat) appointing the person empowered to file the incorporation dossier via the Guichet Unique
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Legal representative of the corporate shareholder or a public notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, accompanied by a sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial owner register extract or signed beneficial owner declaration of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholder's statutory auditor, notary, or the pertinent UBO registry of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization with sworn French translation; original company stamp required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity card of the manager (gérant) and each individual beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport or identity issuance authority of the individual's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy or certified true copy with sworn French translation; apostille only if expressly required by the French filing authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement issued within the last three months) for each individual UBO and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated bank in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sworn French translation; apostille generally not required for private address proof

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory ongoing screening of all managers and UBOs against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN (for USD payment clearing), TRACFIN guidance, and French ministerial asset-freeze orders issued by the Ministry of Economy; Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined in CMF Article L.561-10, including family members and close associates, are subject to enhanced due diligence with source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification; additional screening against high-risk jurisdictions per GAFI/FATF and EU delegated regulation lists; screening must be repeated continuously and at no longer than daily intervals in the 60-day pre-incorporation period.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique); preliminary name availability checks conducted through data.inpi.fr and Infogreffe search services.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) must be expressed in Latin characters; where a foreign name is used, a French transliteration and a French registered office address must be stated; the name must be lawful, distinctive, not misleading, and not identical or confusingly similar to an existing RNE entry, trademark, or protected official designation; the letters 'SARL' or the words 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' must be included in the company's official name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: France (when implying an official state entity)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A 30-day internal clearance is applied to the selected name before filing; no automatic extension is available, so a rejected or lapsed name requires a fresh search and refiling. Upon rejection by the INPI/RNE, the applicant may (i) amend the draft articles and submit a new filing; (ii) file an administrative appeal with the INPI General Director within two months of the refusal decision, with grounds based on availability, identity, or distinctiveness; and (iii) pursue judicial recourse before the Paris Court of Appeal (competence for RNE decisions) within two months of the administrative decision. If a prior trademark holder opposes, the matter may additionally be heard by the commercial court or the INPI opposition division.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted under Article L.123-11-1 of the French Commercial Code provided the domiciliation provider is an approved commercial domiciliation company registered with the préfecture; however, for a data-center colocation and bare-metal hosting business, the tax administration and commercial courts require evidence of a physical operational site (lease agreement for rack space, energy supply contract, and supervision arrangements). A virtual registered office is therefore acceptable only as the registered seat, while a genuine operational facility must be demonstrated before commencement of hosting activities to preserve VAT deduction and corporate substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate, approximately 15% probability during the first 24 months; unannounced inspections are authorized by tax and commercial law (in particular the Business Fraud Police and the local commercial court) and are more frequent in the digital infrastructure sector where lease-back and service-abuse risks are screened; a clean operational facility and documentary trail materially reduce inspection risk.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability and distinctiveness search at RNE/Infogreffe plus preliminary clearance report
Drafting of the SARL articles of association (statuts) and shareholder resolutions in French
Sworn French translation of UBO and corporate shareholder documents (standard multi-page bundle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator (traducteur assermenté) registered with the Cour d'appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of the Cour d'appel and prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized legal announcement journal of the department of the registered office

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: INPI / Guichet Unique registration fee and RNE processing plus related greffe taxes
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory INPI fee schedule and regulatory greffe taxes

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial domiciliation (registered office) for the first 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark under Article L.123-11-1 of the French Commercial Code

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign corporate and UBO documents (unit cost per bundle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign ministry, apostille office, or French consulate of the document's country of origin

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of a professional bank account (KYC onboarding fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; waived or reduced in some institutions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register declaration filing and administrative support pending Kbis issuance
AML/CFT PEP and sanctions screening package for all shareholders, managers, and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance technology provider and French legal counsel

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Article L.210-1 et seq. and Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL); Decree No. 2022-1045 on the Guichet Unique for company formalities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS) maintained by the Greffe du Tribunal de commerce; formalities submitted through the INPI Guichet Unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Demande d'immatriculation au registre du commerce et des sociétés (formulaire M0) together with executed Statuts and annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory capital for SARL. The amount is freely fixed in the Statuts and must be fully subscribed. Cash contributions must be deposited in a French bank or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and blocked until registration; in-kind contributions require valuation and, where applicable, a statutory contribution auditor.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the incorporators and initial manager, acting as the first governance body of the SARL, hereby: (i) approve the subscription of all issued shares and the allocation of share capital as set out in the statuts; (ii) adopt the address at [Registered Office Address], France, as the registered office and statutory seat; (iii) appoint [Name] as first Gérant-Manager, with sole and full powers to represent the company, sign banking instruments, and conclude colocation lease agreements; (iv) approve preliminary legal expenses, including publication of the legal notice; and (v) authorize the Gérant-Manager to complete the RCS registration through the Guichet Unique, open bank accounts, and perform all ancillary acts. The resolution passes unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft statutory documents, open capital deposit account, and execute Statuts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique as final coordination portal; depositary bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations for capital blocking.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare French-language Statuts stating the corporate form, share capital, distribution of shares, registered office, duration and manager powers. Open a temporary blocked capital account at a French bank, deposit all cash contributions, and obtain the capital deposit attestation. Have all shareholders, or their duly authorized representatives, sign the Statuts. Where in-kind contributions exceed statutory thresholds, engage a commissaire aux apports to issue the valuation report.
required_dossiers: Draft Statuts (Acte constitutif)
Attestation de dépôt de fonds from the depositary bank or Caisse des Dépôts
In-kind contribution valuation report, if applicable
Identity documents and proof of legal capacity of each shareholder and the manager
Power of attorney, if signatories act through representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the capital deposit attestation is rejected or inconsistent, remedy by obtaining a corrected attestation from the depositary institution, amending the Statuts schedule accordingly, and resubmitting the document package before formal filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the legal notice of incorporation in a Journal d'annonces légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized legal announcements gazette (Journal d'annonces légales) within the jurisdiction of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the constitution notice (avis de constitution) containing the corporate details, registered office, share capital, manager identity and registered trade number to be obtained. Submit the draft to an approved legal announcements publication. After publication, obtain the original issue or an attestation proving publication, which is required for the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Project of the constitution notice
Signed or draft Statuts for cross-checking
Capital deposit attestation number
Proof of domiciliation/registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication office queries or requests corrections, align the notice with the exact wording of the Statuts, republish a corrected avis, and obtain a publication certificate before the expiration of the legal filing deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the incorporation dossier with the INPI Guichet Unique along with the M0 form
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique, which transmits the dossier to the Greffe du Tribunal de commerce for entry in the RCS.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the unified M0 registration form online at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr. Attach the signed Statuts, capital deposit certificate, legal publication certificate, proof of registered office domiciliation, identity and residence documents for the manager(s), a completed declaration of non-conviction and of beneficial ownership, and any necessary powers of attorney. Validate and submit the dossier electronically; the portal will send an acknowledgment of receipt with a tracking number.
required_dossiers: Completed M0 form
Final signed Statuts
Capital deposit attestation
Legal publication certificate from the JAL
Proof of address of the registered office or domiciliation contract
Identity documents and declarations of non-conviction for managers
Beneficial ownership declaration
Power of attorney, if the filing is made by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is returned as incomplete or non-conforming, use the Guichet Unique online regularization window to upload missing documents and correct details. The registry may extend the legal review period; upon confirmation of compliance the application is forwarded to the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain RCS registration and issuance of Kbis extract and SIREN/SIRET identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce, acting through the RCS, and INSEE for identifiers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Greffe validates the statutory and procedural conformity of the dossier, the company is assigned a registration number and is entered in the RCS. INSEE issues the SIREN, SIRET and NIC numbers. The Greffe delivers an extrait Kbis proving the legal existence of the company. Review the Kbis for accuracy of company name, legal form, capital, manager and registered office.
required_dossiers: The complete filed dossier and acknowledgment of receipt
Kbis application automatically generated from the RCS entry
Valid proof of payment of any publication or third-party costs, if payable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe raises a reservation or conditions inscription, provide the requested justification or supplementary document within the set deadline. In case of a formal refusal, appeal to the Presiding Judge of the Tribunal judiciaire or the commercial court's summary proceedings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-formation operational, tax, social, insurance and site-compliance registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique for tax/administrative notifications; DREAL and local authorities for environmental and building permits; CARSAT/DIRECCTE for occupational health and safety registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Kbis, open the final corporate bank account, register for value-added tax and corporate income tax through the Guichet Unique, and complete employer/URSSAF formalities if employees are hired. Confirm that the premises comply with the applicable fire-safety and structural standards. If the data center equipment or energy capacity exceeds ICPE thresholds, file the required registration or declaration with DREAL before operations begin. Obtain the relevant civil liability insurance, and for leased data center space, enter into colocation agreements reflecting B2B service terms and service-level agreements.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
Statuts and any subsequent instruments
Lease agreement or building title for the data center
Environmental compliance files (ICPE registration/declaration, if applicable)
Fire safety and structural load certification reports
Insurance policies covering property damage and liability for colocation services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If environmental or occupational safety clearance is contested, implement remedial measures through a chartered engineer, submit a revised compliance report to DREAL, and request an inspection or a formal regularization order. The company may not begin operation of regulated equipment until the applicable clearance is obtained.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: DREAL (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement) and the local Prefecture; building permits issued by the competent municipal authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: ICPE registration or declaration under Rubrique 2936 (data centers and server hosting installations) and, where applicable, a building permit (permis de construire) for construction or conversion of the data center premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique and DREAL
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (enregistrement) under ICPE Rubrique 2936 where applicable; a full environmental impact assessment is required only for installations exceeding the thresholds set by Article R.122-2 of the French Environmental Code, otherwise a simpler environmental registration or declaration is accepted.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with ICPE emission limits for combustion plant, generator exhaust gases, noise and waste water. No untreated cooling water may be discharged. Refrigerant leakage shall conform to EU F-Gas Regulation (EU) 517/2014. Waste batteries, electronics and coolants must be separately collected and disposed of under approved waste management contracts. Boundary noise levels and generator operation periods must respect local municipal and DREAL permit conditions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS) and commission de sécurité where the building is open to the public; structural load inspection by a certified engineering office; occupational health and safety registration with CARSAT/DIRECCTE; electrical installation verification; and establishment of an internal emergency and staff safety plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); online portal: impots.gouv.fr; corporate incorporations filed via the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, operated by INPI); customs and EORI administration: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (douane.gouv.fr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident-owned French SARL: (1) file formation through the Guichet Unique, receiving the SIREN (national company ID) and SIRET (establishment ID); (2) the competent SIE opens the corporate tax file and issues the French VAT intra-Community number (FR + 2-digit key + SIREN) and a personal tax identification reference (n° fiscal); (3) obtain the EORI number (FR + SIREN) from Customs before moving goods; (4) where a foreign entity is not established in France, form CA 3557 must be filed with the DGFiP Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE) — suppliers established outside the EU must appoint DGFiP-approved fiscal representation under CGI Art. 293 G, and no de minimis threshold applies to services connected with French immovable property.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation default for SARL: profits are taxable to the company under French corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) at 25% standard rate (15% reduced rate on the first €42,500 of annual profit for SMEs meeting the turnover and ownership conditions). France applies its territoriality principle (Territorial_Scope): the IS generally covers French-source profits only, with foreign-branch profits exempt (subject to ATAD CFC rules). No general tax-exempt zone applies; the SARL is not pass-through by default.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no US-style check-the-box election. A one-person or family SARL satisfying CGI Art. 239 bis A / 239 bis AA conditions may elect income-tax transparency (régime des sociétés de personnes), making profits taxable in shareholders' hands; the election is filed with the SIE and locks in for at least five years. For all other entities, entity-level IS is mandatory. EU ATAD hybrid-mismatch provisions are implemented in the French General Tax Code and neutralize mismatches (deduction/non-inclusion or double deduction) involving French residents, overriding elective outcomes; no direct election to create hybridity is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée) — French value added tax, harmonized under EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC and codified in CGI Articles 256–289.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €25,000 (annual French taxable turnover excluding VAT for service businesses, including data center and colocation services — franchise en base, CGI Art. 293 B); €85,000 threshold for supplies of goods. Registration becomes mandatory in the calendar year the threshold is crossed. Non-established foreign suppliers have no threshold and must register from the first euro for services connected with French immovable property or supplies to French non-taxable persons; a taxable person below the threshold may voluntarily register (option for taxation, Art. 293 C CGI).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured B2B electronic invoicing (facturation électronique) applies under a phased French mandate: large enterprises and mid-size enterprises (ETI) from 1 September 2026, SMEs/TPEs from 1 September 2028 (CGI Art. 289 bis). Invoices must comply with the EN 16931 semantic standard (Factur-X or UBL) and be transmitted via the Public Facturation Portal (PPF) or certified dematerialization partner platforms (PDPs), which forward e-invoice and transaction data to DGFiP in near-real time (e-reporting). DGFiP does not pre-clear or stamp invoices; non-transmission or non-conformity triggers procedural fines (€15 per invoice capped by statute) and places input VAT deduction at risk for the recipient.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available where goods are physically exported outside EU customs territory and evidenced as such (exportation exonérée, CGI Art. 262-1-I). For the data center colocation model, dedicated rack/cage leasing constitutes a supply of services connected with immovable property (EU VAT Directive Art. 47, place of supply = France): the SARL must charge French VAT at 20% even to foreign B2B customers; no export zero-rating applies. Pure bare-metal and remote server-management services that confer no right to occupy identified physical space follow the general B2B place-of-supply rule (Art. 44) and are outside French VAT where the customer is a taxable person established abroad, provided the SARL holds documentary evidence of the customer's VAT status, contract, and settlement — such services are effectively exported services but are excluded from French VAT rather than zero-rated, and no French input VAT credit arises on the corresponding revenues except through the ordinary deduction mechanism.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/Déclaration administrative unique, lodged electronically through the DELTA system) evidencing the 'EX' export procedure, exporter identity and physical exit of the goods
Bill of Lading (Connaissement maritime) or Air Waybill (Lettre de transport aérien) proving dispatch outside the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (Attestation de rapatriement des devises / bank statement evidencing settlement of the export receivable within the statutory currency-control deadline)
Commercial invoice and packing list (Facture commerciale et liste de colisage)
Intrastat dispatch declaration for intra-EU movements and, where applicable, dual-use or strategic export licences for server/network equipment crossing EU borders
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export exemption and reverse-charge positions are priority audit targets of DGFiP and French customs. Failure to substantiate an export triggers re-assessment of 20% French VAT, late-payment interest at 0.20% per month, and penalties: 40% for inaccuracies without bad faith, 80% for bad faith, fraudulent maneuvers, or abuse of right (CGI Arts. 1729 and 1729-0 A). Clawback extends to wrongly deducted input VAT credits, and the right of recovery runs three years, extended to six years for concealed activities and up to ten years for fraudulent schemes (LPF Arts. L. 169, L. 176 and L. 187). Criminal tax fraud penalties reach five years' imprisonment and a €500,000 fine (natural persons, increased for legal persons) under CGI Art. 1741; customs false-declaration sanctions include confiscation of goods and fines computed on the customs value (Code des douanes Arts. 410 et seq.). All supporting export documents must be retained until the expiry of the recovery period to avoid retrospective clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) in its capacity as national central bank and balance-of-payments statistical authority, together with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury, Ministry of Economy and Finance) as the competent foreign-exchange and foreign direct investment (FDI) screening authority; legal basis: Code monétaire et financier (CMF) and EU Regulations on free movement of capital.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current-account and capital-account transactions. France fully liberalises capital movements under Article 63 TFEU; profits of an FR SARL may be remitted without exchange-control approval. Operative frictions are limited to (i) the monthly balance-of-payments statistical declaration to the Banque de France for any cross-border transfer exceeding EUR 7,500 (Bic-Open reporting system), and (ii) the prior authorisation regime applicable to non-EU investors acquiring control of a French entity active in a sensitive sector listed in CMF Articles L151-3 and R151-3. A pure Tier-3/4 rack, power and space leasing activity aimed at commercial tenants is not automatically captured by the sensitive-sector list; however, the same activity may trigger authorisation where the hosted infrastructure contributes to public safety, national defence, electronic communications, or the protection of information systems. There is no limitation on dividend remittance beyond standard corporate formalities: statutory audit, shareholder approval of financial statements, and availability of distributable reserves.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France imposes no surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation obligation on export proceeds, whether received in EUR or in foreign currency. Foreign-currency receivables remain freely usable by the SARL, subject only to the Banque de France statistical report for each flow exceeding EUR 7,500 (due by the 15th day of the following month) and to the accurate statement of the transaction purpose code on the underlying MT103 or SEPA instruction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (compte professionnel) with segregated Capital Escrow Account in EUR/USD
Operational Account (compte courant) with USD nostro clearing and trade-finance desk
Operational Account with SEPA Direct Debit (ACH-equivalent) collection engine
Operational Account plus LC/MT103 issuance capability
Operational Account optimised for non-EU counterparty flows

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility as a secondary collection rail, but Low as the primary treasury and clearing anchor. EU-licensed electronic-money institutions operating under CMF Article L522-1 (e.g., Qonto SAS, Wise Europe SA, Revolut Business, Shine) can provide French IBANs, SEPA Credit Transfer, SEPA Instant, SEPA Direct Debit, and commercial-rate FX conversion. However, they are not credit institutions: they cannot legally hold client funds in escrow, cannot open a conventional capital-escrow account, and are not covered by the Fonds de Garantie des Dépôts et de Résolution (FGDR) in the same manner as bank deposits. For a capital-intensive colocation business relying on escrow commitments and monthly SWIFT inflows, EMIs should be limited to low-value, high-frequency receivable collections; settlement-grade balances must remain with an ACPR-licensed credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally possible under CMF Article L561-5 where the bank applies eIDAS-compliant electronic identification or certified documentary verification, but Tier-1 French banks in practice require for non-resident directors and UBOs: (i) a physical KYC interview held in France or at the bank's EU operating branch, or (ii) a notarised and apostilled identity package accompanied by proof of address issued within the last three months. The KYC interview is effectively mandatory in any case where a natural person residing outside the EEA holds more than 25% of the SARL. The bank must verify the SARL's Kbis/RNE extract, the registered office, the UBO declaration registered in the Registre National des Entreprises, and the signatory powers. Foreign directors without a French tax number or French address have no fully digital alternative in practice; a physical visit or a bank-accepted French-issued certified identity solution is required before account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque non-resident ownership chain preventing identification of ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RNE-registered UBO declaration; consolidated organisation chart down to natural persons; notarised and apostilled passport copies of each UBO; share register; source-of-funds statement signed by all shareholders covering the initial capital injection and future equity contributions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear commercial substratum of the colocation lease model creating a risk of acting as a payment or shell company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed colocation head-lease or usufruct agreement proving physical asset nexus; customer contract template containing rack, power and cooling service-level descriptions; pro-forma invoices; forecasted cash flows; detailed explanation of monthly billing and data-centre operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential ML/TF exposure through the tenant base (crypto-mining, unlicensed payment aggregators, opaque SaaS platforms).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written AML/CTF client acceptance policy; crypto and TF screening procedure; sub-tenant due-diligence questionnaire; negative-news and sanctions screening outputs; IP-reputation checks; contractual right to suspend services immediately upon discovery of sanctioned or unlawful activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and embargo sensitivity of cross-border counterparties, including non-EU tenants and shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ongoing compliance screening against EU consolidated sanctions, OFAC and UN lists; sworn declarations from all tenants confirming the absence of sanctioned beneficial ownership; contractual termination clauses; bank-requested sanctions attestation letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FDI authorisation ambiguity for a non-EU parent investing in a French digital-infrastructure entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion confirming that the rack-leasing activity does not fall within the sensitive sectors of CMF R151-3; where any doubt exists, a complete pre-injection submission to the Direction Générale du Trésor; commitment letter stating that no national-security data hosting will be performed; statistical FDI declaration filed after the injection.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections by the non-EU shareholder must reference the Banque de France balance-of-payments purpose code for equity contributions to a resident company and the payment narrative 'apport en capital social'; the beneficiary must be the SARL with its French IBAN. The physical transfer is executed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202. Prior to the injection, the non-EU investor must assess whether the SARL's effective activities are captured by the French FDI screening mechanism (CMF L151-3 / R151-3); a pure rack-leasing activity normally falls outside the list, but an ex-ante authorisation request is mandatory if the site serves or hosts systems contributing to critical public services or national security. After crediting, the SARL must complete the capital-increase filing with the Guichet Unique within one month and file the statistical FDI report with the Banque de France where applicable. Shareholder loans from abroad are routed via MT103 with the purpose code 'avance en compte courant d'associé' and must respect arm's-length interest to avoid French thin-capitalisation and deemed-dividend recharacterisation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Revenue collection: intra-EU tenants settle by SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant; extra-EU tenants settle monthly invoices via SWIFT MT103. Disbursements: (i) facility, power and cooling vendors by SEPA Direct Debit or SEPA Credit Transfer; (ii) international hardware and network suppliers by MT103, or by sight or standby commercial letters of credit issued in EUR or USD under UCP 600 (SWIFT MT700) where documentary compliance is required; (iii) clearing of USD invoices through the bank's USD nostro account with same-day value-date instruction. Each outbound transfer exceeding EUR 7,500 must be reported to the Banque de France via the Bic-Open portal by the 15th of the following month; no exchange-control approval is otherwise required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable OTC FX forwards in EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and EUR/CNH, executed under EMIR clearing and bilateral margin rules with a licensed counterparty
FX swaps and forex rollovers for short-term working-capital conversion between EUR and USD
OTC European-style FX options (call and put on EUR/USD and EUR/CNY) to cap conversion risk on USD-denominated colocation tariffs

Cross-currency swaps between EUR and USD for long-term infrastructure debt servicing, provided the bank is an ACPR-licensed credit institution and the instrument qualifies as a hedging derivative under IFRS 9
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for currency pairs lacking a liquid deliverable offshore market; NDFs are not customary for EUR/USD and are not recommended

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) shareholder approval and filing at the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (INPI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after fiscal year-end; shareholder approval must occur within 6 months and filing within 1 month after approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers court-ordered fines of up to EUR 50,000 for the legal entity, revocation of tax benefits on undistributed profits, and potential compulsory publication order; no automatic strike-off but repeated default may result in commercial registry removal proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporation tax return (déclaration de résultats) and related schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers: May 3 (paper), May 15 (EDI), June 30 (EDI teleservice); for non-calendar fiscal years: within 3 months after close of financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% on assessed tax plus monthly interest of 0.20%; willful omission attracts 40%–80% penalties; no strike-off consequence but can trigger tax recovery proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS) via Guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following any change in direct or indirect ownership or control; not an annual-cycle filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 10,000 and disqualification from corporate management; false declarations carry criminal penalty up to EUR 10,000 and/or 6 months imprisonment; no strike-off effect

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general meeting agenda, quorum, and minutes archive
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company statutory registers (minutes retained within company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Convened and held within 6 months after close of each financial year; minutes signed and archived immediately after the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting and authenticate minutes invalidates the accounts approval process; managing director and shareholders become jointly liable for any resulting audit or registration refusal

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business property tax declarations (contribution économique territoriale / contribution foncière des entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) – local tax department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Various declarations due in May–June for the following assessment period; actual property values must be reported every year via localised forms
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty 10% of payable tax plus interest at 0.20% monthly; possible property tax reassessment; no strike-off consequence

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registered office/agent and compliance statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INSEE Statutory Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At any point during the year when mandatory filings or changes occur; no fixed annual renewal date under French law
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update reflects inaccurate registration; may lead to fines up to EUR 10,000 and refusal of certified company documents; no automatic strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when a French limited-liability company (SARL) exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total balance sheet assets over EUR 2,000,000; net turnover excluding VAT over EUR 4,000,000; average permanent workforce over 50. Smaller SARLs are exempt unless legal or shareholder requests are made.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) as prescribed by the Code de Commerce and the Autorité des Normes Comptables; IFRS is required only for consolidated accounts of listed groups and certain public companies, not for a standalone SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual direct confirmation exists under French law; instead, the SARL must file an updated beneficial-owner declaration with the RCS within 30 days of any share transfer, control change, or change in details. The annual general meeting verifies the completeness of the share register and the managing director certifies the UBO statement as part of the annual accounts filing package when a change has occurred.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) rate for fiscal years closing on or after 1 January 2022; 15% reduced rate applied to the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs with turnover below EUR 10 million
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for SMEs; Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% for SME innovation expenditure up to EUR 400,000; accelerated depreciation for certain energy-efficient data-center cooling and IT equipment; CVAE (territorial value-added contribution) fully abolished from 1 January 2024; 5-year deficit carryback credit (report en arrière) under Article 220 quinquies CGI

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire n°2065-SD (CERFA 11085) and supporting liasse fiscale (forms 2050–2059); mandatory electronic filing via the EDI-TDFC tele-declaration module on impots.gouv.fr professional portal or through an approved EDI partner
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending on 31 December: the second working day following 1 May of the following year. For any other fiscal year-end: the second working day after the expiry of three months following the close of the fiscal year. The balance of the corporate income tax (solde de l'IS) is payable by direct debit on 15 May, or on the 15th day of the month following the statutory filing deadline for off-calendar fiscal years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre A - Box 'Résultat net comptable – Bénéfice (A)'
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit before tax per French GAAP (PCG), as drawn from the approved annual accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL files this return irrespective of the non-resident status of its shareholders; a non-resident legal representative may sign only if the entity holds a French SIRET and the return is digitally certified by the appointed fiscal representative where no French manager exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of non-deductible expenses and tax-driven adjustments linking accounting profit to taxable income, including depreciation recapture and disallowed royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the arm's-length principle to intercompany rack-space leasing and bandwidth fees paid to foreign affiliates; deductions will be denied if contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is not substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 'Déficit de l'exercice reportable en arrière'
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Election under Article 220 quinquies CGI to carry a current-year loss back against prior-year taxable profits, generating a refundable tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The carryback credit may be offset against future quarterly instalments; a detailed computation schedule must be attached to the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Page 3 - Box 'IS brut puis IS net après imputation des crédits d'impôt'
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross corporate income tax computed at 25% or the reduced 15% rate, then net tax after offset of CIR, CII and the deficit carryback credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits of the ultimate non-resident owner are not claimable on the SARL's return; treaty relief is invoked only through the withholding tax procedures at distribution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic 10% penalty on the unpaid tax; 40% if recovery is not effected within 30 days of a formal demand (mise en demeure); 80% for fraudulent maneuvers. Late payment accrues a 0.20% monthly surcharge plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month (2.4% annualized). Formal omissions on the return give rise to fixed fines up to EUR 10,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire n°2571-SD (quarterly instalment declaration and payment of corporate income tax) via the EDI-TDFC tele-declaration module; instalments may be settled by direct debit (prélèvement) or SWIFT wire to the DGFiP collection account.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year taxpayers: instalments are due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December. For off-calendar fiscal years: each instalment is due on the 15th day of the month following each three-month period from the fiscal-year opening. No instalment is payable when the estimated annual tax is zero; the balancing payment is due with the 2065-SD annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit of the previous fiscal year used as the instalment base; each instalment equals 25% of the estimated annual corporate income tax before credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A SARL beneficially owned by non-residents must pay all instalments from a French bank account in euros; a fiscal representative may be required where the entity is controlled by a non-resident person.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset against the instalment due of available CIR/CII credits and the 5-year deficit carryback credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits must be substantiated on demand; a foreign head office may not carry back the losses of its French branch to its own residence country.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Underpayment of a quarterly instalment relative to the final assessment triggers a 20% penalty on the shortfall, increased to 40% when the shortfall exceeds 10% of the amount due at the deadline and the total due exceeds EUR 60,000 (Article 1730 CGI), plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.20%.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory withholding tax under Article 119 bis CGI on dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the parent holds at least 10% of the SARL's capital for at least two years and both companies are genuinely established in the EU; for individual non-resident shareholders, a 30% flat levy (12.8% tax plus 17.2% social contributions) applies subject to treaty reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Protocol to invoke DTA relief: (1) the non-resident shareholder obtains an official Tax Residence Certificate (TRC / attestation de résidence fiscale) from its home tax authority; (2) the TRC is delivered to the French paying SARL together with Form 5000 (and Form 5001/5002 for individuals) before the distribution date so that the reduced treaty rate can be applied at source; (3) for EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, the parent must complete Form 2561 certifying the 10% minimum holding and the two-year holding period; (4) if the full 25% domestic withholding was nevertheless deducted, the non-resident shareholder must file a refund claim (réclamation contentieuse) with the DGFiP no later than 31 December of the second year following the year of withholding, attaching the TRC and evidence of beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic royalty withholding: 33⅓% under Article 182 B CGI on patent, trademark and similar IP royalties paid to non-residents; 0% for copyright and software royalties paid to residents of the EU/EEA under Article 182 B bis. DTA rates commonly reduce royalty withholding to 5%–10% (e.g., France–US: 5% for industrial royalties). Interest: no domestic withholding on ordinary arm's-length interest paid to non-residents; a 75% withholding applies to interest paid to entities established in a Non-Cooperative State under Articles 125 A III and 238-0 A CGI; the EU Interest and Royalties Directive exempts interest and royalties between associated EU companies holding 25% or more of the SARL's capital for at least two years.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 consolidated group turnover or total assets (Article L.13 AA LPF) triggers the mandatory preparation and filing of the French Master File and Local File documentation together with the electronic transfer pricing declaration on Form 2257-SD; groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000 must additionally file the Country-by-Country Report on Form 2258-SD. All documentation must be supplied to the DGFiP within 30 days of a written request.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies no registration-based Economic Substance Regulation of the UAE/offshore type; substance is instead enforced through the General Anti-Abuse Rule (abus de droit, Article L.64 LPF), the recharacterization provision of Article 155 A CGI for artificial leasing/service structures, and the BEPS MLI Principal Purpose Test when treaty relief is claimed. A data-center colocation SARL must demonstrate genuine premises, operational staff, active server management and decision-making in France; an empty shell without local substance will be disregarded, its intercompany deductions denied, and its income re-taxed at 25% without treaty reduction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting monthly rack-space lease invoices and bare-metal server hosting revenue from Form 2065-SD, booking fictitious depreciation on non-existing colocation equipment, or filing a false simplified tax declaration to avoid the normal reporting regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 80% bad-faith penalty (majoration pour manœuvres frauduleuses) on the evaded tax plus 0.20% monthly late-payment interest; criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 and 5 years' imprisonment under Article 1741 CGI, increased to EUR 1,000,000 and 7 years when committed by an organized group; mandatory publication of convictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or caused the false return are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt under Article L.267 LPF; criminal courts may order restitution, confiscation of data-center assets, travel bans, and disqualification from managing a French company; in insolvency proceedings, directors face 'comblement du passif' for faute de gestion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a zero-substance French SARL with no staff, no local decision-making power and no French bank account solely to route colocation lease income to a tax-haven parent, while claiming DTA benefits on dividend outflows without genuine economic activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGFiP invokes Article 155 A CGI and re-taxes the entire lease income in the hands of the true French beneficiary at 25% plus the 80% fraud penalty and interest; DTA relief is denied under the MLI Principal Purpose Test; administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 apply for failure to disclose the effective beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who established the artificial shell face personal liability for the full corporate tax shortfall, asset sequestration, travel bans, and up to 5 years' imprisonment for aggravated tax fraud when the shell is stripped of its capital before assessment.
